To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the majority of clinicians in a large national network of Operational Stress Injury (OSI) clinics in Canada reported that they regularly used a routine outcomes monitoring and feedback system (ROM-FS), but actual usage was lower than reported.

the implementation of a routine outcomes monitoring system in an operational stress injury clinic network was successful, and that the implementation process was influenced by a range of barriers and facilitators.

1) The majority of clinicians report regular use of routine outcome monitoring, but objective data suggest lower actual use; 2) Clinicians endorse all barriers and most of the facilitators as having a minor influence on their use of routine outcome measurement; 3) Users and non-users differ in the extent to which they endorse the facilitators and barriers; 4) The majority of users endorse the routine outcome monitoring system as useful, but non-users do not.

understanding the nature of social support, its relationship to psychological well-being and its potential for enhancing mental health service utilization.
the development, implementation and evaluation of a system for the routine collection, monitoring, and feedback of patient-reported outcomes in an operational stress injury clinic.

we have developed an effective and efficient system for the routine collection and use of client reported outcome measures in an integrated health system.
the use of a routine outcome monitoring system in a national mental health network can be implemented with some success, although the system may be underutilized.

routine outcome monitoring can be implemented in a national network of operational stress injury clinics and can be useful to clinicians in the provision of care.
routine outcomes monitoring can be successfully implemented in an operational setting, with some barriers and facilitators to be taken into consideration in future implementation efforts.
the use of routine outcomes measurement is not only feasible in a national network, but that it can be implemented in a way that is acceptable to clinicians and clients.
